items.section: Explicit disposal, destructor cleanup, and the gap between them
items.text: Game::Dispose() calls Dispose(true), which returns early when already disposed, and then raises Disposed unconditionally, so every repeated Dispose() re-raises the event; a Disposed handler that calls Dispose() recurses without bound.
items.note: XNA 4.0 (IL of Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Game) also raises Disposed on every disposing call from Dispose(bool) with no guard, and CNA's GameTests comment calls the shape FNA-faithful; the Known Issues pipeline may classify this as intended compatibility behaviour rather than a defect.

items.section: Explicit disposal, destructor cleanup, and the gap between them
items.text: isDisposed_ is set only after all Dispose(true) cleanup; an exception from a component, the ContentManager or the device service (including an UnloadContent override inside DeviceDisposing) aborts the rest, leaves the game un-disposed and suppresses Disposed; the next Dispose() restarts from the first component, and an UnloadContent that threw is invoked again because the manager sets its own disposed_ last.

items.section: Explicit disposal, destructor cleanup, and the gap between them
items.text: ContentManager::Unload() is a single loadedAssets_.clear(); no cached IDisposable asset is disposed explicitly. Game::Dispose(true) reaches it through ContentManager::Dispose(true). Whether native resources leak depends on each asset type's copy/ownership semantics (Load<T> returns by value), which was not traced.
items.note: No-disposal is still present; the leak consequence is unclear from reading.

items.section: ResetElapsedTime() under fixed timestep
items.text: ResetElapsedTime() sets forceElapsedTimeToZero_ only when IsFixedTimeStep is false, so under the default fixed step it does nothing; XNA 4.0's ResetElapsedTime sets its flag in both modes (and resets running-slowly counters) and its Tick zeroes the elapsed time before branching, so a blocking load followed by ResetElapsedTime produces a catch-up burst (up to 29 updates) in CNA but not in XNA.

items.section: IsRunningSlowly: five-tick hysteresis
items.text: IsRunningSlowly uses an FNA-style lag counter (set at 5 accumulated extra steps, cleared at 0) that no test pins; XNA 4.0 uses a different rule (two multi-step ticks within 20 ticks, assigned before each Update), so behaviour can diverge tick by tick and no oracle comparison exists.

items.section: The override points
items.text: Game::ShowMissingRequirementMessage is declared virtual but nothing in CNA calls it; XNA 4.0's Game.Run offers NoSuitableGraphicsDeviceException and NoAudioHardwareException to it before rethrowing.

items.section: Properties, and one that is deliberately not settable from outside
items.text: InactiveSleepTime is validated and stored but never applied; an inactive CNA game keeps its normal rate, whereas XNA 4.0's Tick sleeps for InactiveSleepTime while inactive.
items.note: Already recorded as a gap on development/internals/runtime/module.html#state.

items.section: GameComponent and DrawableGameComponent: the update/draw ordering contract
items.text: GameComponent::Dispose(true) raises Disposed but does not remove the component from Game.Components; XNA 4.0's GameComponent.Dispose(true) removes it first, so XNA code that disposes a component to retire it leaves it updated and drawn in CNA.

items.section: GameComponent and DrawableGameComponent: the update/draw ordering contract
items.text: DrawableGameComponent loads content once in Initialize and never subscribes to the device service (OnDeviceCreated is dead code; no DeviceDisposing hook), unlike XNA 4.0 which reloads on DeviceCreated and unloads on DeviceDisposing and requires an IGraphicsDeviceService.

items.section: GraphicsDeviceManager's role in the loop
items.text: GraphicsDeviceManager::FindBestDevice, RankDevices and CanResetDevice are never called by the manager; overriding them has no effect on device selection.

items.section: Explicit disposal, destructor cleanup, and the gap between them
items.text: Game::Dispose(true) walks Components by index re-reading the count instead of a snapshot (XNA 4.0 copies to an array); a component whose Dispose removes itself or another component shifts later entries and the next component is skipped by that pass.

items.section: Format and fullscreen preferences: three fields, three kinds of truth
items.text: The comment in GraphicsDevice::applyPresentationParametersToWindow describes fullscreen failure as non-fatal, but neither it nor GameWindow::EndScreenDeviceChange catches; on SDL3 a refused request throws PlatformException out of ApplyChanges/CreateDevice (Reset restores its presentation state). Stale comment; whether throwing is the intended contract is undocumented.

items.section: Vertical retrace is a presentation preference, not the fixed timestep
items.text: The Vulkan renderer was described as ignoring runtime swap-interval changes (FIFO kept after vsync is disabled).

items.section: What happens when a frame runs long
items.text: The zero-first-update rule is applied only on the fixed-step path; in variable step the first update receives the interval since Run() seeded the counter, while the XNA values recorded in GameClockFirstUpdateTests' variable-step comment imply zero elapsed time for XNA's first two variable-step updates. The test asserts only the total-lag relation.

items.section: The timing loop, ported wholesale from FNA
items.text: On Emscripten an exception thrown by a frame is caught and logged, the loop ends without raising Exiting, and Run() returns normally, so the game's caller cannot observe the failure.

items.section: Game: base class, not framework-owned entry point
items.text: ExitingEventArgs is constructed nowhere (Game::Exiting uses EventArgs, matching XNA 4.0, which has no ExitingEventArgs type); CNA's AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md use EventHandler<ExitingEventArgs> Exiting as an illustrative event declaration, which differs from the real one.

items.section: GameWindow: one concrete class where FNA has a hierarchy
items.text: GameWindow::getIsBorderlessEXTProperty/setIsBorderlessEXTProperty carry the EXT suffix but not the CNAEXT marker, so CNA_STRICT_XNA_API does not flag them.

items.section: GameComponentCollection: an event-raising collection, plus a real C++ iterator surface
items.text: GameComponentCollection's CNAEXT non-const iterators expose the raw pointer storage; assigning through them bypasses ComponentAdded/ComponentRemoved and Game's ordered lists.

items.section: Explicit disposal, destructor cleanup, and the gap between them
items.text: ContentManager.hpp documents System::ObjectDisposedException for use after disposal, but the implementation throws std::runtime_error("ContentManager has been disposed.").

items.section: Supporting cast: LaunchParameters, TitleContainer, TitleLocation, FrameworkDispatcher
items.text: LaunchParameters parses the program path as an argument; a Windows path with a drive letter (C:\...) yields a spurious key 'C'. On macOS, iOS and the web the game's LaunchParameters is always empty.
